Consult Summary:
- Patient with known heart failure presents with worsening shortness of breath and bilateral ankle swelling over the past weeks, most pronounced in recent days; heart failure exacerbation suspected. Plan includes increasing diuretic, arranging blood tests and echocardiogram, and close follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Increasing shortness of breath over the last two weeks, significantly worse over the past few days.
- Symptoms: Now breathless at rest and on minimal exertion (walking to shops, around the house); required to sit down to catch breath. 
- Associated symptoms: Mild, non-troublesome dry cough; bilateral ankle swelling noted over the last few days; feeling somewhat run-down but otherwise well.
- No chest pain, no palpitations, no fevers, no reduced appetite.
- No urinary complaints aside from chronic frequent urination since starting diuretic.
- Previous similar episode of ankle swelling with prior heart failure decompensation.
- Systems review: No other symptoms or system involvement reported.

Past Medical History:
- Heart failure: Diagnosed previously, managed with Furosemide and additional medications; prior episode of increased breathlessness and ankle swelling resolved with treatment.
- Prior myocardial infarction ("small heart attack") approximately 5 years ago; no complications reported since.
- Medications:
    - Furosemide (dose/route/frequency not documented; currently to be increased to one tablet twice daily)
    - Aspirin (dose/route/frequency not documented)
    - Bisoprolol (dose/route/frequency not documented)
- No known medication allergies.

Social History:
- Lives alone with two cats (Polly and Tim).
- Employed part-time as a daytime lorry driver; finds work exhausting. Concerned worsening health may affect ability to work.
- Exercise: Walks to the shops daily; previously more active.
- Smoking: Former smoker, approximately 1 pack/day for 25 years; quit (date not specified).
- Alcohol: Does not drink alcohol.
- No recreational drug use mentioned.

Family History:
- Father: Died of heart attack in early 60s.
- Mother: Alive, has osteoporosis.
- No other relevant family history reported.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: "Chest, saturations and blood pressure are all OK" (exact values not provided).
- No further physical findings documented.

Investigations:
- No tests or imaging results available at present.
- Plan for blood tests (full blood count, renal function) and echocardiogram (to be arranged).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Worsening heart failure symptoms (increased breathlessness, ankle swelling)
  - Increase Furosemide to one tablet twice daily for a few days
  - Monitor response to increased diuretic
  - Advise to contact doctor sooner if condition worsens (breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, dizziness)
- Issue 2: Need for reassessment of cardiac function and exclusion of other causes
  - Order blood tests (full blood count, kidney function)
  - Arrange echocardiogram to reassess heart function
- General plan items:
  - Schedule follow-up appointment in one week
  - Encourage patient to seek earlier review if symptoms deteriorate

Quality checks:

●	Missing but clinically expected elements: Exact medication dosages and frequencies, full current medication list reconciliation, baseline functional status, more comprehensive review of systems, date of smoking cessation.
●	Internal transcript conflicts: None identified.
●	Transcript quality: Clear and complete; some sections contain minor interruptions but essential clinical data present.
